suleymaniye.text: In the name of Allah, whose goodness is boundless and whose generosity is abundant...[1]

notes.1: The words "Rahman" and "Rahim" are from the root of mercy (رحمة). Mercy means a subtlety that necessitates goodness and generosity. When used as an attribute of Allah, only goodness and generosity are understood (Mufradat). Rahman means "whose mercy encompasses everything." Since this attribute cannot be found in anyone other than Allah, we translated this word as "whose goodness is boundless." Rahim means "very merciful." Since this attribute can also be found in beings other than Allah, we gave it the meaning of "abundant generosity." Indeed, the word 'Rahim' is used for the Messenger of Allah in the verse [Tawbah 9:128] and for the believers in the verse [Al-Fath 48:29].

suleymaniye.text: To do everything perfectly[1] is exclusive to Allah, the Lord[2]/Owner of all beings.

notes.1: "Praise" is to praise someone for what they have done. Statements like "He cooks well, he is a good friend" fall under this. "Gratitude" is to praise someone who has done you a favor or to reciprocate a favor with a favor (Lisan’ul-arab). Only Allah does everything beautifully. We used the word "perfect" instead of "beautiful" to show the difference between what Allah does and what people do.
notes.2: The translation of the word "Rabb = Lord" is "owner." The owner of the house is called rabb’ud-dâr = the lord of the house (Müfredât), and the owner of the capital is called rabb’ul-mal = the lord of the capital. Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) said to the slave sent by the king: "Go back to your Lord and ask what the problem was with the women who cut their hands?" "My Lord knows their schemes." ([Yusuf 12:50]) In this verse, the word "Lord" is used first in the sense of "the king who owns the slave," and then in the sense of "Allah, the owner of everything."

suleymaniye.text: The One Whose goodness is boundless, whose generosity is abundant,[1]

notes.1: For the meaning of the words Rahman and Rahim, see: [Fatiha 1:1]. Footnote of the verse.

suleymaniye.text: The Day when everything will be recompensed[1] belongs to Allah, the sole authority of the Day.[2]

notes.1: The expression translated as "the Day when everything will be recompensed" is "Yevm'ud Din," which means "the Day of Judgment." The word "Deen" means "custom, situation, reciprocation of deeds, recompense, and obedience/submission" (Sihah). In the Quran, "Deen" also means the system that man accepts and promises to live according to ([Al-i Imran 3:19], [Kafirun 109:6]). In Allah's religion, only Allah is to be obeyed. The "Day of Judgment" is the Day of Hereafter when the recompense for what was done in the world will be received ([Nur 24:25], [Saffat 37:19]-20, [Sad 38:78], [Al-Zariyat 51:6] 12-13, [Al-Waqi'ah 56:56], [Al-Ma'arij 70:26], [Al-Muddathir 74:46], [Al-Infitar 82:9], 15-19).
notes.2: On the Day of Judgment, Allah is the only authority. On that day, no one will have the power to do anything in favor of another ([Al-Hajj 22:56], [Al-Furqan 25:26], [Al-Zumar 39:43]-44, [Al-Mu'min 40:16], [Al-Jasiyah 45:27], [Al-Infitar 82:17]-19).

suleymaniye.text: (O Allah!) We worship You directly[1] and we seek help directly from You[2]

notes.1: The word we have translated as "worship" is "ibadah (عبادة)". In Arabic, worship means to bow down by considering oneself at a lower level (Mufradat). In general, however, when worship is mentioned, only duties such as prayer, fasting, and zakat come to mind. Therefore, in the translation, the expression "worship" reflecting the broad meaning of the word in Arabic has been used. In many verses, it is stated that people worship individuals or beings that they place between themselves and Allah. But Allah Almighty does not accept such worship ([Tawbah 9:31], [Yunus 10:18], [Zumer 39:3]).
notes.2: To seek help directly from Allah is to not put an intermediary between oneself and Him when asking for something ([Al-Jinn 72:20]). Because some consider Allah to be in an unreachable position, and they seek help through an intermediary whom they perceive as close to Allah ([Zumer 39:3]), thus elevating that intermediary to the level of divinity. However, Allah is closer to man than his nerve endings ([Kaf 50:16]). In fact, because they feel this, when they are in distress, they forget the intermediaries and turn directly to Allah, seeking help from Him. But when their troubles pass, they turn to the intermediaries again ([Enam 6:63-64], [Isra 17:67], [Ankabut 29:65]-66). People can ask each other for help. Because Allah has commanded cooperation in goodness and piety/avoiding wrongdoing; and He has forbidden cooperation in sin and enmity ([Al-Maidah 5:2]), and also indifference towards someone who asks for something ([Duha 93:10]).

suleymaniye.text: Guide us to the straight path[1];[2]

notes.1: Sirat-i Mustaqim means "the straight path". Being on this path is only possible by worshipping Allah. ([Al-i Imran 3:51], [Yasin 36:60]-61). Worshipping only Allah is possible by adhering to His book. ([Al-An'am 6:151]-153, [Zuhruf 43:43]).
notes.2: The direct equivalent of the expression translated as "Guide us to the straight path" is "guide us to the straight path". Guidance is to gently show the way (Mufradat). Allah's guidance is of four types: Firstly; showing His existence, unity and closeness to everything on every occasion. Therefore Allah warns those who go astray in some way ([Al-Shams 91:8]-10, [Al-An'am 6:125]). He considers it polytheism to see Allah as inaccessible and to place intermediaries between oneself and Him, and He never forgives this behavior ([Al-Nisa 4:48], [Al-Nisa 4:115]-117). Secondly, He guides man, to whom He has given the ability to distinguish good from evil, in finding the truth ([Anfal 8:29]). Thirdly, He guides through the books He has revealed. Therefore, each of those books is a guide ([Al-Baqarah 2:2], [Al-Baqarah 2:38]). Fourthly, He accepts everyone who makes the right choice into His path and confirms that they are on the right path ([Ibrahim 14:4]).

verses.arabic: صِرَاطَ الَّذ۪ينَ اَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْۙ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّٓالّ۪ينَ

suleymaniye.text: Guide us to the path of those whom You have bestowed Your favor upon[1] and those who have not deserved Your wrath[2] and have not gone astray[3]. (Amen)[4]

notes.1: The words "Rahman" and "Rahim" are from the root of mercy (رحمة). Mercy means a subtlety that requires kindness and generosity. When used as an attribute of Allah, only kindness and generosity are understood (Mufradat). Rahman means "whose mercy encompasses everything." Since this attribute cannot be found in anyone other than Allah, we translated this word as "whose goodness is infinite." Rahim means "very merciful." Since this attribute can also be found in beings other than Allah, we gave it the meaning of "abundant generosity." Indeed, the word "Rahim" is used for the Messenger of Allah in the verse [Tawbah 9:128]; [Fath 48:29]. In the verse, it is used for believers.
notes.2: Anger is the equivalent of "gazab" in Arabic. Those who deserve anger, in light of the relevant verses, are: Some Jews ([Al-Baqarah 2:61], [2:90]; [Ali-Imran 3:112]; [Al-Ma'idah 5:60], [Al-Araf 7:152]), those who intentionally kill a believer ([Al-Al-Nisa 4:93]), those who resist the truth ([Al-Araf 7:71]), those who flee from the battlefield ([Al-Anfal 8:16]), those who apostatize ([Al-Nahl 16:106]), those who commit excesses ([Taha 20:81]), those who engage in unjust arguments about Allah ([Al-Shura 42:16]), those who slander their husbands to clear themselves while being unchaste.
notes.3: Those who go astray are: those who deny the verses of Allah ([Mu'minun 23:105]-[23:106]), those who disbelieve after believing ([Al-Maidah 5:12]), those who hinder from the path of Allah ([Al-Nisa 4:167]), those who exceed the limits in religion ([Al-Maidah 5:77]), those who follow conjecture ([Enam 6:116]), those who prefer the life of this world to the life of the hereafter ([Ibrahim 14:3]), those who associate partners with Allah ([Al-Nisa 4:116]), the transgressors ([Al-Maidah 5:108]; [Al-An'am 6:77]), those who pray to others besides Allah ([Ahkaf 46:5]; [Hajj 22:12]), those who take devils as their protectors between themselves and Allah ([Araf 7:30]), the oppressors ([Maryam 19:38]), those who rebel against Allah and His Messenger ([Ahzab 33:36]), those who take a rigid stance against the remembrance/book of Allah ([Zumer 39:22]), those who do not accept the call of Allah's callers ([Ahkaf 46:32]), those who deny the Day of Judgment ([Shura 42:18]), the hypocrites ([Al-Baqarah 2:8]-16), those who conceal the books revealed by Allah ([Al-Baqarah 2:174]-175]), the disbelievers ([Al-Nisa 4:136]), the polytheists ([Al-Nisa 4:116], [Ibrahim 14:30]), those who are captivated by worldly possessions and adornments and stray from the truth ([Yunus 10:88]), those who follow their own desires ([Yusuf 12:30]), those who stray from the Book of Allah ([Taha 20:52], [Luqman 31:6]), those who follow those who speak about Allah without bringing any evidence from the Book of Allah ([Hajj 22:8]-[22:9]), those who befriend the wicked ([Furkan 25:28]-[25:29]), those who deny the truth ([Qalam 68:7]-[68:8]).
notes.4: Amen, "O Allah, accept it!" said after the prayer. It is a word in the sense of (Lisanu’l-Arab). The word does not appear in the Quran. It is narrated that our Prophet said "Amen" after finishing the Fatiha while leading the prayer, and he asked the congregation to also say "Amen" (Bukhari, "Tafsir", 2; Muslim, "Salat", 62, 87).
